author: Josh Unsworth
body: The our scouts have found Spices of the most unusual kind: the bark of a tree which, when dried and powdered or cooked with food, gives an unusual sweet taste.

options.text: There is so much to learn about the flora of the world.
The people of our city are soon making new treats with the spice.
Gift the families with supplies to spice their drinks.

title: A Bitter Bark to Bite

author: David Ballantyne
body: The bountiful harvest of Fur is far too much to be sold in our people alone, but perhaps merchants in our people would be willing to buy our excess?

options.text: Let our people enjoy our Fur, for a price of course.
I’d rather the Fur rots than our people benefit from our work!

title: A Fortune in Furs

author: Josh Unsworth
body: Among the Jade is a colossal piece, of a size that would make the most monumental of statues. If it can be transported, that is. Moving such a stone will take time, co-ordination, and a whole lot of effort. Luckily you can order others to do it for you.

options.text: Order it hauled to our city.
Make the extra effort to transport it to our city.
Break it apart to be easily carried.

title: A Green Giant

author: Andy Auseon
body: Thanks to the recently discovered cache of gold, ministers in our city plan to fund the construction of a new royal treasury. Of course, this windfall may be better spent on the people than on ourselves.

options.text: I welcome another place of royal wealth.
Our people deserve the wealth of knowledge.

title: All that Glitters

author: Andy Auseon
body: One of the elephants in the newly discovered herd appears to have been domesticated. It wears a saddle and military ornamentation. Perhaps we can remind the beast of its training.

options.text: Let the beast live a peaceful life in a city zoo.
Train the beast to lead our troops in battle.

title: Beast of Burden

author: Velociryx
body: Word has reached your ear of an enterprising young woman, who hit upon a new fermentation technique not long after harvesting wild grains. This new technique has allowed her to brew ale of a potency that far surpasses anything your men in the field have sampled previously.

options.text: She's brilliant. Let's give this woman a job!
Lovely! Bring this ale back to our city so we can all enjoy it.
Interesting, but I'm more interested in the grain itself. Order the men to bring back seeds so we can plant fields near our city.

title: Beer Run

author: Andy Auseon
body: Our scout was bitten while corralling a caravan of camels, and he will need to take some time to recover from his injury. This particular breed of creature has a cruel disposition.

options.text: Have the whole caravan slaughtered for meat.
Give the camels to the Tribe and be rid of them.

title: Camel Bite

author: Andy Auseon
body:
Court scientist the subject recently joined a fishing expedition to research {G2:his:her} latest work, a treatise on marine life and fishing techniques. Unfortunately, {G2:he:she} fell from {G2:his:her} boat, was trapped in a tangle of nets, and {G2:he:she} was prodded with many barbed tridents before {G2:his:her} rescue.

The poor {G2:man:woman} has suffered numerous misfortunes, but perhaps we can ease the pain.

options.text: Allow the subject to publish {G2:his:her} treatise.
Send {G2:him:her} on a royal research expedition.
Build {G2:him:her} a fishery to practice new methods.

title: Capsized

author: David Ballantyne
body: As our Scouts organise the herd of Elephants for their drive to our city, they point out that such large creatures can surely carry a lot of resources. It would be quite easy to bring along a load of Wood or Stone, depending which you would prefer.

options.text: Wood.
Stone.

title: Carrying Capacity

author: Andy Auseon
body: Our scout was recently caught pilfering a wagonload of newly discovered silver, and he is now brought before the court for justice. The man pleads for his life, hoping that a life of service to the throne will be enough to earn his freedom.

options.text: These crimes cannot go unpunished.
He is more valuable doing his duty.

title: Caught in the Act

author: Andy Auseon
body: Scientists in our city claim that eating citrus fruit can help combat the withering effects of a long sea voyage. It is a controversial position, but one worth considering. Our scout's latest harvest of citrus could take the usual route into the hands of local merchants, or we could divert it to the shipyards and sailors.

options.text: Our brave crews should have them.
This remedy has not yet been proven.

title: Citrus Remedy

author: Josh Unsworth
body: You watch, transfixed by the slow progress of the tiny creature as it worms its way across your hand. The our scouts have sent back a number of the creatures, claiming that it is these that produce the Silk, not the trees it is found on.

options.text: Keep the creatures to yourself, to see how they grow and thrive.
Send them to the academics for study.
Gift the larvae to our city to cultivate new sources of Silk.

title: Cocoon Couture

author: Andy Auseon
body: The style of marble recently discovered has fetched a high price in the local bazaars, and noble families wish to raise prices to corner the market. What shall we tell merchants?

options.text: Reduce the price so more can afford it.
Raise prices to ensure its rarity.

title: Corner the Market

author: David Ballantyne
body: The flock of sheep has been driven to our city and we must decide what to do with them. They could simply be slaughtered for food, or the flock could be allowed to graze and provide benefits over the long run.

options.text: We need the food now!
Allow them to graze.

title: Counting Sheep

author: David Ballantyne
body:
Our Scout has developed a strange theory after observing a consortium of Crabs. He has come to the conclusion that crabs have the ideal form and that over a long enough time scale, all life will develop into a more crab-like form.

As a result, he recommends our military leaders study these crabs and learn from them.

options.text: It’s unconventional, but give it a try.
What nonsense, cook them up!

title: Crab Controversy

author: Solver
body: Our scouts have harvested some particularly delicious grapes. You've had quite a few drinks in your life, but the wine prepared from these grapes is better than any. It's certainly too good to go to waste!

options.text: Arrange for feasts in our city, keep that wine flowing!
Make sure the nobles get a good supply of this deliciousness!

title: Delicious Wine

author: Josh Unsworth
body: No sooner has the Ebony found by the our scouts entered into our city, than the Religion {S3.PRIEST,2} start trying to lay claim to the exquisite wood. They clamor that the dark material is perfect for the inscriptions that accompany tombs.

options.text: Give them the Ebony that they desire.
Send the precious material to market.
Organize for craftsmen to inscribe the wood for them too.

title: Divine Price

options.text: EVENTOPTION_CALAMITIES_DROUGHT_TRIBE_HARVEST_WAR
EVENTOPTION_CALAMITIES_DROUGHT_TRIBE_HARVEST_APOLOGIZE
EVENTOPTION_CALAMITIES_DROUGHT_TRIBE_HARVEST_SHARE

author: Josh Unsworth
body:
The the family family have complained about the woodland being cut down around our city, claiming that the area was a vital hunting spot for the the family nobles.

Your advisors are sure that the subject is just pushing the point in an attempt to receive compensation from the crown coffers.

options.text: Give them the compensation they seek.
Invite them to come and hunt around our city.
Plant the seeds of new woodlands.

title: Family Trees

author: Josh Unsworth
body: Cutting through the trees, the our scouts discover a flock of vivid green birds. Managing to capture one, they have presented it to you as a gift, claiming that such creatures are capable of mimicking human speech.

options.text: What a fascinating creature!
This would make a fine gift to improve relations with the subject.
Catch them all. We’ll make a fortune.

title: Feathered Friend

author: David Ballantyne
body: A terrible mishap has caused over 30 recently caught wild pigs to escape and run loose around our city, presenting a grave danger to local children. How can they be best killed?

options.text: The army could use some target practice!
Tell the people they may eat any pig they kill.

title: Feral Hogs

author: Andy Auseon
body:
Several days after shepherding a group of wild goats to the palace, the goatherd falls ill. Various members of his family also get sick. It seems the goats have brought disease with them.

Now the subject exhibits similar symptoms. We should act fast to contain this potential outbreak.

options.text: The cooks should dispose of all meat in the kitchens.
the subject must remain isolated.
We must study this sickness to learn all we can.

title: Filthy Animals

author: David Ballantyne
body: The herd of goats has been driven to our city and we must decide what to do with them. They could simply be slaughtered for food, or the herd could be allowed to graze and provide benefits over the long run.

options.text: We need the food now!
Allow them to graze.

title: Getting Goats

author: Andy Auseon
body: Examining the latest salt harvest, scientists and merchants recognize the potential for large-scale salt production for food preservation and nutrition. the subject, governor of our city, requests that we provide funds from the treasury to develop this process for {G2:his:her} city.

options.text: Proceed with research into salt production.
The court cannot fund this project now.

title: Great Potential

author: Andy Auseon
body: Along with the wheat they harvested from the nearby countryside, our scouts return to our city with a group of hardy tribal farmers. These nomads possess a unique knowledge of this particular grain, and they could be put to use on our farms.

options.text: Ask them to share their expertise.
We need hands to work the fields.

title: Helping Hands

author: Andy Auseon
body: Among the fields of twisting grape vines, our scouts meet a wandering scholar who has drunk his fill of the local varietals. The man offers his service to the court, though he may be of more use helping our scouts bring home the harvest.

options.text: Let us try this stranger in the court.
We shall plant more of these fine grapes.

title: High Spirits

author: David Ballantyne
body: A herd of horses will be extremely useful, but should the best specimens be used to carry your messages or to carry your warriors?

options.text: My messages are my weapons.
My warriors are my weapons.

title: Horsing Around

author: David Ballantyne
body: While organizing the camel train, one of our Scouts correctly pointed out that the camels might as well carry some resources back with them. It should be possible to bring either a large load of food or a smaller amount of Iron without slowing their progress.

options.text: Bring Food.
We need Iron!

title: Humping Resources Home

author: Jeri Roys
body:
While bringing down wild game, one of your hunter's arrows strikes a well dressed woman pursuing the same prey. It is soon apparent both that her injuries are not fatal, and that a crest marks her as royal blood of the line of our people!

What do you do?

options.text: Make a legal claim to local hunting rights, and imprison the young noble as a poacher.
Provide for her recovery and send her on her way.

title: Hunting Accident

author: Josh Unsworth
body: Your our scouts report seeing a hulking animal amidst the Resource. Sending one of their number to investigate further, the our scouts soon runs back claiming to have seen <p.is_sub.S3=SUBJECT_PLAYER_EGYPT>a hunting griffon, a giant lion with the head of an eagle<else>a lion large enough to match the one slain by {S4.HERO}<end> as told in the myths of Religion.

options.text: The hunt is on!
Let the legends sleep.

title: Hunting a Myth

author: Andy Auseon
body: With the recent acquisition of fine fur, your {G2:husband:wife} has asked {G2:his:her} servants for the creation of new fashions to showcase the luxury. However, several members of the court wish to use the warm material to outfit our soldiers, who suffer in cold conditions.

options.text: Grant the subject {G2:his:her} desired garments.
Give the fur to our brave soldiers.

title: Luxury or Utility

author: David Ballantyne
body:
The latest fashion for the upper class in our city is to adorn the gates of their estate with beautifully carved marble statues. As the recently discovered marble is of an especially fine quality, it has caused a bidding war of noble families seeking to out-shine their rivals.

Of course, as Title you have the right to decide what is done with it.

options.text: My gate could use a statue.
Give it to the subject as a goodwill gesture.
Sell it to the highest bidder.

title: Marble Madness

author: Andy Auseon
body: Deep in the ore deposits, our scouts unearth a collection of strange and marvelous specimens. Although these impressions resemble fish and birds found in our lakes and forests, they exhibit many strange characteristics.

options.text: We must examine these puzzling remains.
Send the subject to investigate these strange creatures.

title: Marvelous Specimens

author: Josh Unsworth
body:
Although the land is unclaimed by any nation, the wheat is not unattended. Your our scouts are greeted by an elderly man who has looked after the land for as long as he can remember. 

Invited to stop and eat, your people are amazed by the quality of the grain that the reclusive farmer has produced. This is someone who clearly knows their craft.

options.text: Ask about his techniques to train your own farmers.
Invite the farmer to settle in our city.
Accept the meal and set off with a full stomach.

title: Master of the Harvest

author: David Ballantyne
body: The influx of Citrus fruits, which are not only tasty but well-known to counteract poison, into our city has promoted a wave of good health! This in turn will lead to increased growth.

options.text: Good for our city!

title: Medicinal Fruits

author: David Ballantyne
body: Our scouts report finding an abandoned gem mine. There are a number of loose gems which can be easily taken, but there is also a much larger gem further in atop some kind of altar. The scouts report an ominous feeling emanating from the large gem and refuse to touch it without direct orders.

options.text: The small gems will do.
Fools, bring me that large gem!

title: Minor Problems

author: David Ballantyne
body: A sudden glut of Olive Oil in our city presents several opportunities. The army could make use of it for military applications, learned men could investigate additional ways to manipulate it, or we could simply allow the citizens of our city to enjoy the oil themselves.

options.text: Make the army a well-oiled machine.
Lubricate the minds of our researchers!
Let the people use it as they will.

title: Multipurpose Oil

author: Josh Unsworth
body:
People cower in fear as the recently harvested Elephant are led through the streets of our city. The rumors are that these creatures can live for 300 years, bite off the heads of men, and that even their smell strikes fear into horses.

To find such mythic beasts reflects well on your dynasty. The scouts excitedly discuss how they might find a manticore next.

options.text: Use their likeness on our coins as a symbol of power.
Order more research on these fascinating creatures.
To inspire such fear must mean an affinity to the divine.

title: Mythical Beasts

author: Andy Auseon
body: A large supply of fresh olive oil has been pressed with the recently harvested crop of olives. The timing is fortunate. Both our people and our people have developed an affinity for our olive oil, and this rich reserve would make an excellent gift.

options.text: Send the olive oil to our people.
Send the olive oil to our people.
Why waste such a luxury on foreigners?

title: Olive Oil

author: Andy Auseon
body:
Our scouts have encountered a group of experienced pearl divers off the coast. For a small contribution, these brave men and women are willing to add more treasures to our harvest.

Both the the family and the family families have expressed a desire for more pearls. Perhaps this is an opportunity to win favor on the court.

options.text: Fund an expedition and send pearls to the the family.
Fund an expedition and send pearls to the the family.
Support the dive, and I will take the pearls.
We should save that money.

title: Pearl Divers

author: David Ballantyne
body:
News has reached our city that a batch of particularly perfect pearls have been discovered recently. Many local artists have expressed interest in working together to create a beautiful mosaic in the city square with them.

While this would likely attract many admirers, there’s also something to be said for simply selling the pearls and pocketing the money.

options.text: our city the beautiful!
our people the rich!

title: Perfect Pearls

author: Andy Auseon
body:
Somehow, a wild pig has appeared inside the palace. Its squeals fill the corridors, as courtiers and servants scurry for safety!

You suspect that the beast was in the drove of pigs recently brought back to our city from the wilderness. You also suspect that young the subject set it loose.

options.text: I will help my {G3:son:daughter} raise it.
Roast it for a grand banquet.

title: Pig in the Palace

author: David Ballantyne
body: Incense has a wonderful smell, but the question is where to put it to best use. It could be used around your palace, increasing the royal mystique, or it could be used to improve the atmosphere in the more crowded public areas of our city.

options.text: Overawed people won’t dare revolt!
Less revolting people will be happier.

title: Pleasant Scents

author: David Ballantyne
body: With a large harvest of Wine on its way to our city, there are two suggestions for its use. Some advisors think it would be best to keep it for medical use, while others recommend a massive party to improve the mood of the city. Which should it be?

options.text: Medical use.
Throw the party!

title: Put an End to their Wining

author: Andy Auseon
body:
In an attempt to collect more crabs than his nets allow, our scout capsizes his boat and must be rescued by local fishermen.

Afterwards, these friendly gatherers have expressed an interest in migrating to our people to start a new life. Where shall they settle?

options.text: We need fishers in our city.
We need fishers in our city.

title: Rescue at Sea

author: Josh Unsworth
body: The new harvest of Ebony is small, yet enough to fashion into an item worthy of a Title. The royal artisans stand ready, what will you ask for?

options.text: Use it to craft instruments for the court musicians.
Something for your personal use.
Finely detailed pieces for games of strategy and wit.

title: Resonant Instruments

author: David Ballantyne
body:
The rich harvest of Wheat will allow the population of our city to grow faster than ever before.

On the other hand, we could instead add it to our central stockpile, to serve all of our people

options.text: Allow our city its growth!
The needs of the many outweigh the needs of the few.

title: Rich Harvest

author: Andy Auseon
body: The positive effects of the recently harvested incense have made it highly prized by Religion groups. They wish to obtain the entire crop for their ceremonies to keep harmful spirits away, but many in our city wish to use it for the simple purpose of improving daily life.

options.text: Hold the incense for the population of our city.
Allow the Religion to use it for rituals.

title: Ritual Scent

author: Andy Auseon
body:
In the recent harvest, gatherers discover a collection of herbs and flowering plants with a variety of properties. Most striking, however, is how this plant produces a bright red pigment for paints and colored fabric.

Scientists have begun to investigate this herb with earnest, discovering many uses.

options.text: Crimson dyes will enhance our garments and art.
Let us explore cultivating more of this plant.
This herb may hold medicinal properties.

title: Rose Madder

author: Josh Unsworth
body:
Among the recently acquired deer stands a striking buck, a foot taller than the rest and made of muscle. The Religion Magi of our city have asked to sacrifice it to Ahura Mazda at the annual Nowruz feast, but the locals want to put it to breeding to strengthen the herd.

How will you break this stalemate between the Magi and the people?

options.text: It will make a fine sacrifice.
Keep the stag with the herd.
Take it for your own hunting grounds.
Let it go free.

title: Sacrificial Deer

author: David Ballantyne
body: The flow of Salt into our city has spurred a wave of culinary innovation, most notably it has resulted in a delicious sauce made by fermenting the guts of fish in brine. People in our city are already using this sauce in almost all their cooking, and doubtless it will soon spread throughout all our people!

options.text: I must try some!

title: Salty Sauce

author: Jeri Roys
body: Seafood is becoming an increasingly prized delicacy in the capital since being popularized by recent expeditions. This might present an opportunity.

options.text: Profit from the rarity.
Aim to expand operations.

title: Sea for Ourselves

author: David Ballantyne
body:
While out catching Fish, our scout reports seeing a terrible serpent in the water, “its jaws were large enough to admit a man on horseback, and each flake of its horny scales exceeded an oblong shield in length!”

Theories abound as to what this could have been.

options.text: What an amazing creature!
We must be prepared if it poses a danger.

title: Seeing Serpents

author: Josh Unsworth
body: While harvesting the spices, some of the our scouts have been taken suddenly and devastatingly ill. Their recovery reveals that they all ate the same one of the Spices that they recently harvested. This potent plant causes a severe burning that they suggest anyone would be fool to try.

options.text: I will not be defeated by a plant.
I certainly will not be defeated by a plant.
Spice up the dishes of our city with small doses.

title: Some Like it Hot

author: David Ballantyne
body:
While examining the newly-harvested Sorghum seeds by torchlight, a merchant in our city had a fortunate accident. The grains, left too close to the flame, began to burst with loud popping sounds.

After calming down, the merchant discovered this ‘Sorburst’ to be quite delicious, especially with butter, salt, or honey. She now has a thriving business and our city is becoming well known for this delicacy!

options.text: I expect Sorburst stands to pop up all over our people!

title: Sorburst Snacks

author: Andy Auseon
body: Scouts have returned with pouches of sorghum seeds, which will allow us to cultivate the crop locally. Farmers have already begun to sow open fields in our city. For what purpose should they raise this grain?

options.text: our city always needs more food production.
Brew wine and other alcoholic beverages.
Use it to feed animals of field and pasture.

title: Sorghum Seeds

author: David Ballantyne
body: The recent influx of Silver brings with it two possibilities. One choice is to offer silver spurs to our most distinguished messengers, encouraging them to ride harder than ever before. The other is to commission a set of plates and goblets, to gift to the head of the powerful the family family to improve their opinion of your rule.

options.text: The messengers!
The the family family!

title: Spurring Innovation

author: Andy Auseon
body: As our scouts explore the newly discovered gem deposit, they come upon a small band of our people who are also interested in the rich vein. Both groups regard the other suspiciously, and they wait for someone to make the first move.

options.text: Continue with our harvesting.
Offer some of our bounty to the our people.

title: Standoff

author: Josh Unsworth
body:
When harvesting the Horse, your our scouts discover one steed with a coat of pitch-black hair. Standing above all other horses, the steed is so fast that the our scouts agree that he must surely be of divine stock, a stallion fit for the gods.

It takes your people days to capture the horse but eventually it is done. What will become of this noble stallion?

options.text: Let the horse sire a new line in your stables.
Take the horse for yourself.
Send the horse as a gift for the subject.

title: Steed of the Gods

author: David Ballantyne
body: While the obvious use for a fresh batch of Ore is to forge swords and armor, some of our blacksmiths instead wish to use it to experiment with new casting techniques in the hopes of learning something new.

options.text: Swords!
Science!

title: Swords or Science?

author: David Ballantyne
body: Amidst the herd of Deer being harvested, one specimen stands out by having a truly magnificent set of antlers. Its head would make an excellent trophy, even if you didn’t hunt it down yourself.

options.text: Indeed, off with its head!
No, it wouldn’t be right.

title: Taking Trophies

author: Josh Unsworth
body: As they cut through the trees, your our scouts are verbally set upon by a wild {G2:man:woman} who had made the woodland {G2:his:her} home to escape from society. Keeping up a string of insults that leaves the our scouts exhausted, the subject follows the directions they give {G2:him:her} to your palace, boldly coming before you to demand satisfaction. With {G2:his:her} home destroyed, what is to become of the subject?

options.text: It really does not concern me. Cut it all down!
Give {G2:him:her} space to reside on the outskirts of our city.
Bring {G2:him:her} to court.

title: The Ascetic in the Woods

author: David Ballantyne
body: The windfall of gold flowing into our city gives you an opportunity. A new series of coins can be minted, but should they bear your face or honor the brave soldiers who defend our people?

options.text: Me, of course.
Our defenders, no question!

title: The Coin Question

author: Josh Unsworth
body:
The shepherds of our city regularly give the finest of their flock to the Religion temples as a tribute. God demands that sacrifices be 'without blemish', but the shepherds have started keeping the best of the flocks to themselves, and handing over lame and sick sheep instead.

The Religion priests have found this out, and are asking that the shepherds be made to give only those sacrificial lambs that are worthy of God.

options.text: Give the finest of the shepherds flocks to the priests.
Allow the shepherds to continue.

title: The Lame and Sick

author: David Ballantyne
body: We have discovered a source of rich purple Dye, a most unusual colour. Purple garments would be a sign of great prestige, so the question is, who should be allowed to wear them?

options.text: I, and only I!
I will also allow the the family family to wear purple.
Anyone who can afford them, may wear them.

title: To Dye for

author: Andy Auseon
body: The game here has a tough, sinewy texture, and the flavor leaves much to be desired. However, when boiled and treated, the animals' insides can be used for many practical purposes.

options.text: Research new uses for these products.
Breed more of them for their parts.

title: Tough Game

author: Josh Unsworth
body: As cinnamon is gathered and sent back to our city, the merchants of the city have come up with a cunning way to protect their trade. They are claiming to foreigners from our people that the spice is harvested from unknown lands by giant cinnamon birds, who collect the bark for their nests.

options.text: Inform the our people of the location the Spices were gathered.
Keep quiet and let the coin flow in.
Change the birds to winged serpents: More danger means a higher price.

title: Trade Secrets

author: Josh Unsworth
body: As your our scouts cut into the first trees, they discover that beneath the unassuming bark the wood of the trees is pitch black. This new type of Ebony has an especially impressive luster once sanded and polished. The our scouts bring you word of the find, eager for the wealth it could bring.

options.text: We will cultivate this precious resource.
Cut them all down.

title: Treasure Within

author: Josh Unsworth
body: Gathering the Silk from the trees, the our scouts are shocked to find that the cocoons have a naturally yellow, almost golden hue. Once pulled apart and woven into material, you can’t help but marvel at the final effect.

options.text: Introduce the fabric to the merchants of our city.
Subtly introduce the golden silk into your clothing.
I will have the finest outfits ever seen.

title: Webs of Gold

author: Andy Auseon
body: When the recently discovered horses reach our city, your servants inquire as to how the beasts should be used. There is always a need for work animals in the capital, but the decision of how they will be used remains, as always, with you.

options.text: Provide them to military trainers.
Give them to farmers to work the fields.
Harness them for war.

title: Wild Horses

author: Andy Auseon
body: As our scout herds the recently discovered sheep, he discovers a young girl tending to the animals. She appears to be Tribe child who has wandered far from her tribe. She is alone but for her small, loyal flock.

options.text: She may come to our city with her sheep.
She will be given a proper childhood.
She must be returned to the Tribe.

title: Young Shepherd
